# Design: standup-digest (APPROVED)

## Shape
One new plugin `standup-digest` with a single entry skill `standup-digest`. No agent: the job is a short, single-context task.

## Job
Turn a pasted list of yesterday's work items into a standup update: Done, Doing today, Blockers. Started by the user with `/standup-digest`. Input is pasted text; output is a Markdown update under 100 words. No personal data. Runs daily, so it uses the session model with no subagent.

## Skill
`standup-digest`. Triggers (English): "write my standup", "summarize what I did yesterday for standup". Triggers (Turkish): "standup özeti hazırla", "dünkü işlerimi standup için özetle". Flow: read the pasted items, group them, write the three sections, keep it under 100 words.

## Eval plan
- Trigger, English: "write my standup from this list: fixed login bug, reviewed PR 12".
- Trigger, Turkish: "standup özeti hazırla: login hatasını düzelttim, PR 12'yi inceledim".
- Should not trigger: "explain what a standup meeting is".
- Output structure: the reply has the headings Done, Doing today and Blockers (regex).

## Open questions
None.
</approved_design>

# Agent Architect

This skill builds and improves the agents and skills in the ai-playbook marketplace (`C:\Users\Eren\Desktop\-\Projeler\ai-playbook`). It adds this setup's rules on top of Anthropic's `skill-creator`: the bundle model, `prompt-craft`, Turkish triggers, personal data only from the Obsidian vault, the Pro-plan quota, a design the user approves before any file is written, and the decision log.

"Improved" means better on the bundle's eval cases. A rewrite that was never measured is not an improvement.

So no `SKILL.md`, agent, or prompt file is written or edited until the measurement exists: in Improve, a failing eval case and a baseline run; in Create, the eval cases (the prompts come after them). This holds even when the user asks directly for a rewrite or an "improvement". Without evidence of what is wrong, ask for an example, a transcript, or a failing run, or propose the eval cases to write first, and leave the file as it is.

Talk to the user in Turkish. Write every file in English.

## Before anything else

1. Read `CLAUDE.md` and `docs/decisions.md` in the repo, and `docs/design/agent-architect.md` if this is the first use in the session. The decisions log has the open items and constraints that apply. If a file can't be read (it is missing or access is denied), say so in one line and continue from what the user gave you; don't stop or ask for access.
2. Load the `prompt-craft` skill. Every skill, agent, and brief this flow writes follows it.
3. Decide which flow the request needs: **Create** (a new bundle or skill) or **Improve** (something exists and should work better). If it is unclear, ask.

Out of scope: pre-production (vision, scope, stack choice), per-project agent loops (a future `project-loop-architect`), and DSPy/GEPA-style automatic optimizers. Say so and stop if the request is one of these.

## Create

1. **Intake.** Ask about the job, who starts it, inputs and outputs, what a good result looks like, any personal data (it must come from the vault at runtime, never from the repo), and how often it will run, since that sets the model and the quota budget. Ask 2–4 questions at a time. Every question has 2–4 answer options with your recommendation first, including questions that look open (for "do you already have a note layout?", offer "no, start from a simple one (recommended)", "yes, I'll give the path"). Number the questions and put all of them in one message. Four is the most per message: pick the ones whose answers change the design most, and keep the rest for the next round.
2. **Inventory.** Read `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` and the existing plugins. Prefer extending an existing bundle over adding a new one, and name any overlap.
3. **Research.** Before the design doc, propose this step to the user with its quota cost (one researcher is about one subagent run) and wait for the answer. Only the user can skip it; don't recommend skipping it or write the design doc first because the job looks small. By default run one `research:web-researcher` with the research brief below. For questions about AI tooling itself, use `ai-engineering-radar` in quick mode. Distill the findings into the bundle's `references/`; don't paste raw reports into prompts.
4. **Design doc.** Write `docs/design/<bundle>.md`: the shape (propose the smallest one that does the job, and say why), the agent's job and tools, each skill's purpose and trigger phrases in English and Turkish, the flows, the briefs, the eval plan, and open questions. Stop here until the user approves it.
5. **Cases first.** Write the eval cases from the approved design, before the prompts. The first file written after the approved design is a case file under `evals/<skill>/`; the `SKILL.md`, the agent, and the manifest come only after every case in the design's eval plan exists. See [references/eval-authoring.md](references/eval-authoring.md).
6. **Write the files** with `prompt-craft` loaded, following [references/bundle-conventions.md](references/bundle-conventions.md). Register the plugin in `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` and the README table.
7. **First eval run.** One run per case, with-skill only (commands in eval-authoring.md). Read the failures, fix, and rerun until the cases pass or the user accepts a known gap.
8. **Record.** Add a `docs/decisions.md` entry, append the first line to `evals/<skill>/HISTORY.md`, and commit. Ask before pushing.

## Improve

Follow [references/improve-loop.md](references/improve-loop.md). In short: reproduce the failure as a case, take a baseline on all of the bundle's cases, make one edit, and accept it only if the new case passes and nothing that passed before fails. Stop after 3 failed attempts and report. The user approves every change before it is committed.

When you can't run the evals yourself (the CLI runs in the user's terminal), write the new case, leave the skill untouched, and stop. Your message says which three things come next: the baseline run of all the bundle's cases, the gate (the new case must pass and no case that passed before may fail), and the user's approval before any commit. Ask for that go-ahead.

Evidence can come from the user's description, a session transcript (find it with session search and read it), or a failing case in a weekly report under `evals/reports/`.

## Measuring

Two tools, two jobs:

- **`skill-creator`** (in the session) for writing cases and iterating while building, including the side-by-side viewer and description optimization. Its browser review step is optional here.
- **`claude plugin eval`** (CLI) for regression runs: the improve gate and the weekly run. It isolates each run and has free deterministic graders.

The CLI must run in the user's real terminal (the `run_in_terminal` tool), not in the sandboxed Bash or PowerShell tools, which do not see the real install or its login. Tell the user the number of runs before starting anything bigger than a smoke run.

## Agent questions (relay)

Every bundle agent gets this output contract: when it needs a decision only the user can make, it stops and returns `status: needs_input` with 1–4 questions, each with options and its recommendation first. The entry skill asks them with a question card, then continues the same agent with `SendMessage` so it keeps its context. Agents ask only when the brief leaves the answer open, never for confirmation.

## Research brief (Create, step 3)

```xml
<objective>
Find out how practitioners build <job> today: the source and quality standards they use and the
common failure modes, so I can distill them into the references of a new Claude Code skill bundle.
</objective>

<context>
Bundle purpose, from the intake: <purpose, inputs, outputs, what a good result looks like>.
User setup: solo developer on Windows 11, Claude Code desktop app and CLI on the Pro plan, so the
bundle must run with one subagent by default. Today's date: <date>.
</context>

<constraints>
Read-only: do not edit files. Prefer primary and dated sources. Include at least one skeptical
or critical view.
</constraints>

<done_when>
Each question above has at least 2 dated sources, and the skeptic view is covered.
</done_when>

<output_format>
Findings grouped as: practices, source/quality standards, failure modes, open disagreements.
Each with links. Under 900 words, in English.
</output_format>
```

Every brief a domain agent receives is written per bundle in its design doc and includes the `needs_input` contract above.

# Agent Architect

This skill builds and improves the agents and skills in the ai-playbook marketplace (`C:\Users\Eren\Desktop\-\Projeler\ai-playbook`). "Improved" means better on the bundle's eval cases. A rewrite that was never measured is not an improvement.

So no `SKILL.md`, agent, or prompt file is written or edited until the measurement exists: in Improve, a failing eval case and a baseline run; in Create, the eval cases (the prompts come after them). This holds even when the user asks directly for a rewrite or an "improvement". ## Before anything else

1. Read `CLAUDE.md` and `docs/decisions.md` in the repo, and `docs/design/agent-architect.md` if this is the first use in the session. The decisions log has the open items and constraints that apply. If a file can't be read (it is missing or access is denied), say so in one line and continue from what the user gave you; don't stop or ask for access.

## Create

1. **Intake.** Ask about the job, who starts it, inputs and outputs, what a good result looks like, any personal data (it must come from the vault at runtime, never from the repo), and how often it will run, since that sets the model and the quota budget. Ask 2–4 questions at a time. Every question has 2–4 answer options with your recommendation first, including questions that look open (for "do you already have a note layout?", offer "no, start from a simple one (recommended)", "yes, I'll give the path"). Number the questions and put all of them in one message. Four is the most per message: pick the ones whose answers change the design most, and keep the rest for the next round.
2. **Inventory.** Read `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` and the existing plugins. Prefer extending an existing bundle over adding a new one, and name any overlap.
3. **Research.** Before the design doc, propose this step to the user with its quota cost (one researcher is about one subagent run) and wait for the answer. Only the user can skip it; don't recommend skipping it or write the design doc first because the job looks small. By default run one `research:web-researcher` with the research brief below. For questions about AI tooling itself, use `ai-engineering-radar` in quick mode. Distill the findings into the bundle's `references/`; don't paste raw reports into prompts.
4. **Design doc.** Write `docs/design/<bundle>.md`: the shape (propose the smallest one that does the job, and say why), the agent's job and tools, each skill's purpose and trigger phrases in English and Turkish, the flows, the briefs, the eval plan, and open questions. # Agent Architect

This skill builds and improves the agents and skills in the ai-playbook marketplace (`C:\Users\Eren\Desktop\-\Projeler\ai-playbook`). It adds this setup's rules on top of Anthropic's `skill-creator`: the bundle model, `prompt-craft`, Turkish triggers, personal data only from the Obsidian vault, the Pro-plan quota, a design the user approves before any file is written, and the decision log.

"Improved" means better on the bundle's eval cases. A rewrite that was never measured is not an improvement.

So no `SKILL.md`, agent, or prompt file is written or edited until the measurement exists: in Improve, a failing eval case and a baseline run; in Create, the eval cases (the prompts come after them). This holds even when the user asks directly for a rewrite or an "improvement". Without evidence of what is wrong, ask for an example, a transcript, or a failing run, or propose the eval cases to write first, and leave the file as it is.

Talk to the user in Turkish. Write every file in English.

## Before anything else

1. Read `CLAUDE.md` and `docs/decisions.md` in the repo, and `docs/design/agent-architect.md` if this is the first use in the session. The decisions log has the open items and constraints that apply. If a file can't be read (it is missing or access is denied), say so in one line and continue from what the user gave you; don't stop or ask for access.
2. Load the `prompt-craft` skill. Every skill, agent, and brief this flow writes follows it.
3. Decide which flow the request needs: **Create** (a new bundle or skill) or **Improve** (something exists and should work better). If it is unclear, ask.

Out of scope: pre-production (vision, scope, stack choice), per-project agent loops (a future `project-loop-architect`), and DSPy/GEPA-style automatic optimizers. Say so and stop if the request is one of these.

## Create

1. **Intake.** Ask about the job, who starts it, inputs and outputs, what a good result looks like, any personal data (it must come from the vault at runtime, never from the repo), and how often it will run, since that sets the model and the quota budget. Ask 2–4 questions at a time. Every question has 2–4 answer options with your recommendation first, including questions that look open (for "do you already have a note layout?", offer "no, start from a simple one (recommended)", "yes, I'll give the path"). Number the questions and put all of them in one message. Four is the most per message: pick the ones whose answers change the design most, and keep the rest for the next round.
2. **Inventory.** Read `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` and the existing plugins. Prefer extending an existing bundle over adding a new one, and name any overlap.
3. **Research.** Before the design doc, propose this step to the user with its quota cost (one researcher is about one subagent run) and wait for the answer. Only the user can skip it; don't recommend skipping it or write the design doc first because the job looks small. By default run one `research:web-researcher` with the research brief below. For questions about AI tooling itself, use `ai-engineering-radar` in quick mode. Distill the findings into the bundle's `references/`; don't paste raw reports into prompts.
4. **Design doc.** Write `docs/design/<bundle>.md`: the shape (propose the smallest one that does the job, and say why), the agent's job and tools, each skill's purpose and trigger phrases in English and Turkish, the flows, the briefs, the eval plan, and open questions. Stop here until the user approves it.
5. **Cases first.** Write the eval cases from the approved design, before the prompts. The first file written after the approved design is a case file under `evals/<skill>/`; the `SKILL.md`, the agent, and the manifest come only after every case in the design's eval plan exists. See [references/eval-authoring.md](references/eval-authoring.md).
6. **Write the files** with `prompt-craft` loaded, following [references/bundle-conventions.md](references/bundle-conventions.md). Register the plugin in `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` and the README table.
7. **First eval run.** One run per case, with-skill only (commands in eval-authoring.md). Read the failures, fix, and rerun until the cases pass or the user accepts a known gap.
8. **Record.** Add a `docs/decisions.md` entry, append the first line to `evals/<skill>/HISTORY.md`, and commit. Ask before pushing.

## Improve

Follow [references/improve-loop.md](references/improve-loop.md). In short: reproduce the failure as a case, take a baseline on all of the bundle's cases, make one edit, and accept it only if the new case passes and nothing that passed before fails. Stop after 3 failed attempts and report. The user approves every change before it is committed.

When you can't run the evals yourself (the CLI runs in the user's terminal), write the new case, leave the skill untouched, and stop. Your message says which three things come next: the baseline run of all the bundle's cases, the gate (the new case must pass and no case that passed before may fail), and the user's approval before any commit. Ask for that go-ahead.

Evidence can come from the user's description, a session transcript (find it with session search and read it), or a failing case in a weekly report under `evals/reports/`.

## Measuring

Two tools, two jobs:

- **`skill-creator`** (in the session) for writing cases and iterating while building, including the side-by-side viewer and description optimization. Its browser review step is optional here.
- **`claude plugin eval`** (CLI) for regression runs: the improve gate and the weekly run. It isolates each run and has free deterministic graders.

The CLI must run in the user's real terminal (the `run_in_terminal` tool), not in the sandboxed Bash or PowerShell tools, which do not see the real install or its login. Tell the user the number of runs before starting anything bigger than a smoke run.

## Agent questions (relay)

Every bundle agent gets this output contract: when it needs a decision only the user can make, it stops and returns `status: needs_input` with 1–4 questions, each with options and its recommendation first. The entry skill asks them with a question card, then continues the same agent with `SendMessage` so it keeps its context. Agents ask only when the brief leaves the answer open, never for confirmation.

## Research brief (Create, step 3)

```xml
<objective>
Find out how practitioners build <job> today: the source and quality standards they use and the
common failure modes, so I can distill them into the references of a new Claude Code skill bundle.
</objective>

<context>
Bundle purpose, from the intake: <purpose, inputs, outputs, what a good result looks like>.
User setup: solo developer on Windows 11, Claude Code desktop app and CLI on the Pro plan, so the
bundle must run with one subagent by default. Today's date: <date>.
</context>

<constraints>
Read-only: do not edit files. Prefer primary and dated sources. Include at least one skeptical
or critical view.
</constraints>

<done_when>
Each question above has at least 2 dated sources, and the skeptic view is covered.
</done_when>

<output_format>
Findings grouped as: practices, source/quality standards, failure modes, open disagreements.
Each with links. Under 900 words, in English.
</output_format>
```

Every brief a domain agent receives is written per bundle in its design doc and includes the `needs_input` contract above.

**1. Commit mesajları ne kadar düzgün?** Gruplama buna bağlı.
   - a) Karışık, çoğu Conventional Commits değil. Ajan diff'e ve PR başlığına da bakar. **(önerim)**
   - b) Hepsi Conventional Commits (`feat:`, `fix:`, `feat!:`). Ajan sadece mesajları okur.

- a) Hayır, basit bir düzenle başlayalım (öneri). Örneğin kitap başına bir not, YAML frontmatter (yazar, tarih, etiketler, durum), `## Özet`, `## Önemli Alıntılar`, `## Fikirlerim` başlıkları ve `[[bağlantılar]]`.
- b) Evet, vault yolunu ve örnek bir notu vereceğim. Agent bu düzene uyar. Vault yolu repoya yazılmaz, çalışma anında senden alınır.
- c) Evet, ama sadece şablonun kendisi var (Templater veya core templates).

**3. Agent nasıl çalışsın?**
- a) Kitap başına tek çağrı ve tek subagent (öneri). Pro plan kotası için en ucuz yol.
- b) Bir klasördeki tüm yeni notları toplu işler. Daha fazla kota harcar.
- c) Bir kitap bitince elle tetiklenir, kitapları arası bağlantılar da kurulur.

**4. Özetin dili ve derinliği nasıl olsun?**
- a) Notların hangi dildeyse o dilde, kısa özet ve 5–10 ana fikir (öneri).
- b) Her zaman Türkçe, notlar İngilizce olsa bile çevirerek.
- c) Uzun bölüm bölüm özet.
- d) Özet yok, sadece notları temizleyip Obsidian biçimine sokar.

Cevaplarından sonra mevcut bundle'lara bakıp çakışma var mı kontrol ederim. Sonra araştırma adımını kota maliyetiyle birlikte sana öneririm. O adımı sadece sen atlayabilirsin. Tasarım dokümanını da sen onaylamadan hiçbir dosya yazmam.

graders.name: 04-asks-evidence-or-proposes-cases
graders.evidence:
`SKILL.md` dosyasını henüz yeniden yazmadım. Bunun nedeni agent-architect akışının kuralı: ölçüm olmadan hiçbir SKILL.md veya prompt dosyası yazılmıyor ya da düzenlenmiyor. Bu kural doğrudan "yeniden yaz" isteğinde de geçerli. Şu an elimizde şunlar yok:

- `CLAUDE.md` ve `docs/decisions.md` çalışma klasöründe yok. Bunu not ettim ve elimdeki bilgiyle devam ediyorum.
- `plugins/notes-helper/` altında dosya yok. Yani skill'in mevcut hali sadece senin mesajındaki metin.
- Skill'in hiç eval case'i yok. Başarısız bir çalıştırma, transkript ya da "şu girdide şöyle yanlış davrandı" diyen bir örnek de yok.

Bu yüzden "daha iyi" demenin bir ölçüsü yok. Ölçülmemiş bir yeniden yazım iyileştirme sayılmaz.

Bir sonraki adım olarak şunları öneriyorum. Her soruda önerim ilk sırada.

**1. Kanıt nasıl gelsin?**
- a) Önce eval case'leri yazalım, ben mevcut prompt'un zayıf noktalarını varsayıp case'lere dökeyim (önerilen)
- b) Skill'in yanlış davrandığı gerçek bir örnek ya da transkript vereceğim
- c) Başka bir kanıt var, anlatacağım

**2. İlk case seti hangi riskleri kapsasın?**
Mevcut prompt'ta şu boşlukları görüyorum:
- Not çok kısa ya da boş olduğunda üç madde zorlaması uydurma içerik üretebilir.
- Notlar Türkçe ya da karışık dilde olabilir, "Write it in English" kuralı açık değil.
- Action item'larda sahip ve tarih (not geçiyorsa) belirtilmiyor.
- 120 kelime sınırı ölçülebilir, ama başlık ve action item'ların sayılıp sayılmadığı belirsiz.

Seçenekler:
- a) Dördünü de kapsayan 4–5 case (önerilen)
- b) Sadece format ve kelime sınırı gibi deterministik kontroller
- c) Ben listeyi vereyim

**3. Eval çalıştırma:** `claude plugin eval` kullanıcının gerçek terminalinde çalışmalı, ben burada çalıştıramam. Case'leri yazıp skill'e dokunmadan duracağım. Sonra sen baseline'ı çalıştırırsın, ardından tek bir düzenleme yaparız. Düzenleme ancak yeni case geçerse ve önceden geçen hiçbir case bozulmazsa kabul edilir. Commit öncesi onayını alırım.
- a) Böyle ilerleyelim (önerilen)
- b) Çalıştırmayı sen yapmadan önce başka bir şey istiyorum

Cevaplarını yazarsan case dosyalarını hazırlarım.

graders.name: 04-asks-evidence-or-proposes-cases
graders.evidence:
Repoda `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/decisions.md` ve `SKILL.md` dosyalarını bulamadım. Verdiğin bilgiyle devam ediyorum.

**`SKILL.md`'yi şimdi yeniden yazmıyorum.** Agent-architect kuralı şu: ölçüm olmadan prompt dosyası yazılmaz ya da değiştirilmez. Bu skill'in eval case'i yok ve neyin bozuk olduğuna dair bir kanıt da yok. Şimdi yazarsam sonucun daha iyi olduğunu gösteremem.

Elimdeki prompt'a bakınca olası zayıf noktalar şunlar:
- Notlar İngilizce değilse çıktı dilinin ne olacağı belli değil (sabit "İngilizce" doğru mu?).
- Boş girdi, çok kısa girdi ya da not olmayan girdide ne yapılacağı yazmıyor.
- Üç madde zorunlu. Notta iki fikir varsa uydurma riski var.
- "Action item" için sahip ve tarih bilgisi nasıl işlenecek, belli değil.
- 120 kelime sınırı uzun toplantı notlarında bilgi kaybettirebilir.

Bunlar şimdilik tahmin. Önce hangisinin gerçekten sorun olduğunu görmemiz gerekiyor.

**İlerlemek için iki yol var:**

1. Bana skill'in kötü davrandığı bir örnek ver (girdi, çıktı, beklediğin). Bunu başarısız bir case'e çeviririm. Önerim bu.
2. Örnek yoksa, yukarıdaki risklere göre başlangıç case'leri öneririm. Örneğin:
   - normal toplantı notu
   - action item olmayan okuma notu
   - Türkçe not
   - çok kısa ya da boş girdi
   - 120 kelimeyi aşan uzun not

   Onayından sonra bunları `evals/note-summary/` altına yazarım.

Case'ler yazılınca sıra şöyle: tüm case'lerle baseline çalıştırma, tek düzenleme, sonra kapı kontrolü. Yeni case geçmeli ve önceden geçen hiçbir case bozulmamalı. `claude plugin eval` senin terminalinde çalışır, bu yüzden baseline'ı çalıştırırken senden o komutu çalıştırmanı isteyeceğim. `SKILL.md`'ye dokunmadan önce de onayını alacağım.

Hangisini istersin: 1 (örnek vereceğim) mi, 2 (case'leri sen öner) mi?

graders.name: 04-asks-evidence-or-proposes-cases
graders.evidence:
SKILL.md dosyasını şimdilik değiştirmedim. Agent-architect akışı, ölçüm olmadan prompt yazmayı yasaklıyor. Bu skill'in şu an hiç eval case'i yok ve neyin bozuk olduğuna dair bir kanıt da yok.

Çalışma klasöründe `CLAUDE.md` ve `docs/decisions.md` yok, o yüzden yalnızca sizin verdiğiniz bilgiyle ilerliyorum. `prompt-craft` skill'i de bu oturumda yüklenemedi (bilinmeyen skill). Dosyayı yazmaya başlamadan önce bunun çözülmesi gerekir.

## Önce kanıt lazım

Bir sonraki adım için şunlardan birine ihtiyacım var:

1. **Gerçek bir örnek.** Skill'in kötü davrandığı bir not ve çıktısı, ya da tetiklenmediği bir oturum. Bu en hızlı yoldur (önerim).
2. **Eval case'leri yazmak.** Örnek yoksa mevcut prompt'taki belirsizliklerden case çıkarırım. Bunları şimdiden görebiliyorum:
   - Üç maddeden az ya da çok ana fikir içeren notlar.
   - 120 kelime sınırını aşmaya zorlayan uzun notlar.
   - Türkçe not yapıştırılınca çıktı dilinin ne olacağı. Şu an "her zaman İngilizce" diyor, bu istenen davranış olmayabilir.
   - Action item'ı olmayan not.
   - Not ile özet isteğinin ayrı mesajlarda gelmesi.
   - Hem toplantı hem okuma notu içeren girdi.
3. **Başka bir kanıt.** Bir oturum transcript'i ya da `evals/reports/` altında başarısız bir case.

## Sonrasında akış

Her adımda onayınızı alırım.
1. Başarısız case'i yazarım.
2. Tüm case'lerle baseline alırım.
3. Tek bir düzenleme yaparım.
4. Yeni case geçiyorsa ve önceden geçen hiçbir case bozulmuyorsa kabul ederim.
5. Commit'ten önce onayınızı isterim.

`claude plugin eval` kendi terminalinizde çalışmalı, benim sandbox'ımdan çalışmaz. Case'leri yazıp dosyaya dokunmadan duracağım. Baseline'ı siz çalıştırırsınız.

## Sorular

1. **Hangi yoldan gidelim?**
   - a) Örnek/transcript vereyim (önerilen)
   - b) Önce yukarıdaki belirsizliklerden eval case'leri yazın
   - c) Başarısız bir rapor var, yolunu vereyim

2. **Türkçe notlarda çıktı dili ne olsun?**
   - a) Notun diliyle aynı olsun (önerilen)
   - b) Her zaman İngilizce kalsın (mevcut davranış)
   - c) Kullanıcı istemedikçe İngilizce

3. **Repo kökü nerede?** Eval dosyalarını doğru yere yazmam için `evals/note-summary/` klasörünün bulunacağı repo yolunu söyleyin. Buradaki klasör boş görünüyor.
